mo-auditor-2026-wilson-quentin.name: Quentin Wilson
mo-auditor-2026-wilson-quentin.bio: Former Director of the Missouri Department of Revenue, Governor's Cabinet Director, Deputy Director of Economic Development, and State Commissioner of Higher Education.

positions.stance: Says the Auditor's office "should be a check on unlimited and unaccountable power, not just a political steppingstone."
Supports "Independent oversight and greater accountability."
Commits to "Listening to all citizens about what matters most to them."
Supports "Promoting more efficient, effective, and transparent government."
Wants to help "public institutions deliver measurable results that make Missouri stronger, safer, and more prosperous."

wi-ag-2026-toney-eric.name: Eric Toney
wi-ag-2026-toney-eric.bio: Fond du Lac County District Attorney since 2013 and former President of the Wisconsin District Attorneys Association.

positions.stance: Pledges to "back the blue, end the revolving door of justice, and make sure violent offenders are off the streets where they belong."
Says he will "go after the cartels, traffickers, and dealers" profiting from fentanyl and meth flooding Wisconsin communities.
Pledges to "modernize our labs, end the backlog, and hold leadership accountable."

wi-ag-2026-kaul-josh.name: Josh Kaul
wi-ag-2026-kaul-josh.bio: Wisconsin Attorney General since January 2019 and former federal prosecutor in Baltimore.

positions.stance: Supports additional state investments to make communities safer and "common-sense gun-safety measures, such as the expansion of background checks for firearms transfers."
Says Wisconsin's AG "should be a watchdog for Wisconsinites and our natural resources," putting their interests ahead of corporate special interests and well-connected insiders.
States "Josh is pro-choice" and cites a ruling that abortions are not broadly banned in Wisconsin by an 1800s-era law.
Describes himself as "deeply committed to protecting our democracy" and has warned against voter intimidation at the polls.
Has joined multistate cases challenging Trump administration actions, including federal funding cuts, tariffs, and the birthright citizenship executive order.

wi-sos-2026-schroeder-jay.name: Jay Schroeder
wi-sos-2026-schroeder-jay.bio: Business leader from Clintonville and former Menomonie City Council member.

positions.stance: "I will fight to make Secretary of State, the chief election official," replacing the appointed Wisconsin Elections Commission's role.
Plans to "Push the Legislature to restore elections to the Secretary of State from the corrupt WEC—by referendum if needed."
Commits to "Implementing rigorous records transparency so every citizen can trust the process."
Wants to remove the "bureaucratic shield" of the WEC so election officials are accountable to the people, not political appointees.

wi-sos-2026-zamarripa-jocasta.name: JoCasta Zamarripa
wi-sos-2026-zamarripa-jocasta.bio: Milwaukee Alderperson for the 8th District and former ten-year member of the Wisconsin State Assembly.

positions.stance: Calls for "bold, statewide investment in affordable child care, attainable housing, and relief at the grocery store."
Believes the state must play a more active role supporting affordable housing development, preventing displacement, and helping renters and first-time buyers.
Supports major state-level investments to expand child care access, improve quality, and pay providers fairly, calling child care "infrastructure."
Fighting for a Wisconsin where "public education is fully funded by the state."
Will ensure Board of Commissioners of Public Lands trust funds supporting schools and libraries "are protected, expanded, and directed to where they're needed most."

wi-treas-2026-leiber-john.name: John S. Leiber
wi-treas-2026-leiber-john.bio: Wisconsin State Treasurer since January 2023; attorney and former legislative staffer and Department of Revenue tax advisor.

positions.stance: Prioritizes growing the Common School Fund, which provides aid for public school libraries and technology and takes pressure off local property taxes.
Has not built a bureaucracy or new programs and has "advocated for fiscal restraint with the Legislature."
Pledges to "do this work, do it well, and do not use the Treasurer's office as a stepping stone."
Says unclaimed money held by the state "is not Madison's to sit on. It should go home."

wi-treas-2026-xiong-yee.name: Yee Leng Xiong
wi-treas-2026-xiong-yee.bio: Marathon County Supervisor, Executive Director of the Hmong American Center, and former DC Everest School Board member and Village Trustee.

positions.stance: Will "prioritize strong returns while protecting the principal" of the Common School Fund and push for transparent, prudent investment strategies.
Supports low-interest Trust Fund Loans for roads, fire stations, school repairs, and infrastructure, including affordable financing for small towns and rural communities.
Wants to "Act as an independent watchdog for Wisconsin taxpayers" and advocate for transparent management and investment of public funds.
Will strengthen efforts to return unclaimed property, expand outreach, and add multilingual resources and modern technology.
Supports balancing "conservation with sustainable revenue generation for education" on state trust lands, with responsible forestry and land management.

co-sos-2026-gonzalez-amanda.name: Amanda Gonzalez
co-sos-2026-gonzalez-amanda.bio: Jefferson County Clerk and Recorder and election attorney who has taught election law at the University of Denver.

positions.stance: "Protect every vote, from every threat"; cites stopping attempts to remove 23,000 voters from Jefferson County's rolls.
"Expand who can vote"; will reach working people, rural and young voters, and voters with disabilities left behind by the system.
"Run elections Colorado can trust"; supports modernizing and streamlining Colorado's TRACER campaign finance system and stronger disclosure.
"Keep Colorado's elections secure"; will keep adding protections against threats such as AI-generated disinformation and federal interference.
Wants business registration, charity filing, and notary systems run by the office to "actually work for the people using them."

co-sos-2026-wiley-james.name: James Wiley
co-sos-2026-wiley-james.bio: Former financial-services practice owner and technology and marketing consultant who has worked full-time on election-integrity efforts since 2020.

positions.stance: Building a "Liberty Coalition across Republicans, libertarians, MAHA warriors, unions, small businesses, families, and unaffiliated Coloradans."
Supports one-day elections as a state holiday, in-person precinct voting, voter ID, "Paper Ballots ONLY," citizen-controlled tabulation, and cleaning the voter rolls.
Will "place all Colorado public records on an immutable blockchain ledger," including voter registrations, property records, business filings, charities, and notaries.
"I will slash red tape" and make it "faster and cheaper to launch and grow a business" in Colorado.

co-treas-2026-bridges-jeff.name: Jeff Bridges
co-treas-2026-bridges-jeff.bio: Colorado state legislator for over ten years, including as Chair and Vice Chair of the Joint Budget Committee.

positions.stance: Running to bring state investment dollars now "parked in Wall Street and Washington" home and put them to work in Colorado.
Supports investing in "Housing that working people like nurses, teachers, and firefighters can actually afford."
Supports investing in "Infrastructure and clean energy that lower your utility bills."
Supports investing in "Colorado companies that create good-paying Colorado jobs."
"As Treasurer, I'll align our investments with our values by investing in Colorado."

co-treas-2026-grantham-kevin.name: Kevin Grantham
co-treas-2026-grantham-kevin.bio: Fremont County Commissioner and former Colorado Senate President (2017–2018).

positions.stance: Wants to "make Colorado a safe and affordable place where anyone that works hard can get ahead."
Says Colorado should get back to being "careful with how it taxes its residents and how it spends their hard-earned tax dollars."

co-ag-2026-allen-michael.name: Michael J. Allen
co-ag-2026-allen-michael.bio: District Attorney for Colorado's Fourth Judicial District (El Paso and Teller counties) since 2020 and U.S. Navy veteran.

positions.stance: Will advocate for laws that put victims first and use the statewide grand jury to investigate organized criminal activity across jurisdictions.
Will conduct "a top-to-bottom review of spending," eliminate waste, and consolidate Attorney General's Office operations to save taxpayer dollars.
Will restore the office "to its role as an independent watchdog" and investigate credible corruption allegations "without fear or favor."
Will "aggressively investigate and prosecute those who prey on Colorado consumers" and expand consumer education on scams.
Will "defend Colorado's water rights, honor our commitments, insist that neighboring states honor theirs, protect our watersheds."

co-ag-2026-griswold-jena.name: Jena Griswold
co-ag-2026-griswold-jena.bio: Colorado Secretary of State (elected 2018, reelected 2022) and former director of the Colorado Governor's Washington, D.C. office.

positions.stance: "Jena is committed to defending our rights and freedoms and fighting for everyone."
Will "safeguard Colorado's natural resources, climate, and fight for middle and working class people."
"Jena believes in fairness and justice."
Will "protect Coloradans and our communities from illegal ICE action and the Trump Administration."

mn-sos-2026-simon-steve.name: Steve Simon
mn-sos-2026-simon-steve.bio: Minnesota Secretary of State; former Assistant Attorney General and Minnesota House member who chaired the House Elections Committee.

positions.stance: Lists "defend our democracy" among his top priorities moving forward.
Priority to "strengthen the freedom to vote for all eligible Minnesotans."
Priority to "push back against dangerous disinformation about our elections."
Priority to "provide support for small businesses."
Priority to "enhance security protections for our most vulnerable."

mn-sos-2026-jude-tad.name: Tad Jude
mn-sos-2026-jude-tad.bio: Former legislator, county commissioner, judge, and small business owner.

positions.stance: "Require a photo ID to vote."
"Ensure only legal U.S. citizens vote."
"Work with local, state, and federal partners to clean up voter rolls."
"Bring back the traditional Minnesota flag by public vote."
"Prevent fraud in public programs."

mn-aud-2026-jensen-scott.name: Scott Jensen
mn-aud-2026-jensen-scott.bio: Family physician in Carver County for 40 years and former Minnesota state senator (2017–2021).

positions.stance: "Go on offense to provide the necessary oversight to prevent and stop fraud."
"Identify and hold accountable fraudulent businesses, agencies, and swindlers."
"Institute internal controls and binding processes to validate service providers."
"Verify the comprehensive ongoing compliance of program recipients of taxpayer dollars."
"Conduct random, unannounced, and ongoing audits of financials and procedures."

mn-aud-2026-filipovich-zack.name: Zack Filipovich
mn-aud-2026-filipovich-zack.bio: Certified Management Accountant, nonprofit finance manager, and former Duluth City Council President.

positions.stance: Supports building staff capacity, relationships with local governments, and "identifying new guardrails where needed to protect against fraud."
Will improve resource sharing, address the shortage of finance professionals in greater Minnesota, and improve the office's data and guidance.
Committed to "holding open houses and forums to ensure transparency at every step" and giving citizens opportunities to be heard.
Using Minnesota law "to take on the drug companies, hedge-fund landlords, and price-fixing schemes driving up costs."
"Keith has no patience for people who steal from taxpayers"; led passage of the MAP Act adding Medicaid fraud investigators and increasing penalties.
Prioritizes going after "gun manufacturers and retailers who ignore the law" and "tech and tobacco companies that target kids."
Says "when Trump violates the laws and harms the people of Minnesota, he can expect to see Keith in court."

mn-ag-2026-schutz-ronald.name: Ronald J. Schutz
mn-ag-2026-schutz-ronald.bio: Trial lawyer and partner in a national litigation firm, which he chaired from 2019 to 2024, and veteran.

positions.stance: "I will make fighting fraud and protecting taxpayer dollars a top priority and take aggressive steps to stop the fraud before it starts."
Pledges to fight for elderly and vulnerable Minnesotans targeted by "powerful individuals and corporations."
"As Attorney General, I will use every tool available to combat crime and protect Minnesotans."
Will "stand with law enforcement, restore respect for those who protect our communities, and ensure officers have the resources and support they need."
Opposes policies allowing "biological males to compete in girls' and women's sports"; will "protect the integrity of girls' and women's sports."

sc-sos-2026-belton-jason.name: Jason Belton
sc-sos-2026-belton-jason.bio: Vice President of the Greater Columbia Central Labor Council and business and nonprofit consultant.

positions.stance: Will "demand total transparency, implement strict disclosure requirements for professional fundraisers, and ensure every dollar you give reaches the front lines."
Will streamline filing and "bring satellite offices to every county, using existing state funded buildings at no additional cost to taxpayers."
Will seek expanded statutory power for the Secretary of State to chair the Election Commission, ensuring transparency and uniform standards across counties.

sc-treas-2026-coe-vincent.name: Vincent Coe
sc-treas-2026-coe-vincent.bio: Trained bank examiner raised in Darlington County.

positions.stance: Pledges "A public report every month on every account, investment and fee the office oversees," with quarterly reports flagging problems early.
Will "Put the state's banking contracts out for competitive bids to bring its fees down."
Will provide better banking and investment help for every county, city, and school district, charging local governments only what the work costs.
Will "Give South Carolina's community banks a fair shot at holding the state's money" and report quarterly how much they hold.
Will "Mail more unclaimed money back to its owners automatically, with no claim form," and post monthly results.

sc-ag-2026-stumbo-david.name: David Stumbo
sc-ag-2026-stumbo-david.bio: Solicitor for South Carolina's Eighth Judicial Circuit and career prosecutor.

positions.stance: Says "the sanctity of life of the unborn, religious liberty, and parental rights must be protected"; advocates lower taxes and transparent government.
Will "protect the rule of law and deliver justice for South Carolina families on Day One as Attorney General."
Will protect crime victims, put criminals behind bars, defend the Constitution, "and keep government power in check."

sc-ag-2026-hricik-richard.name: Richard Hricik
sc-ag-2026-hricik-richard.bio: Attorney who built his own law practice, former tax accountant, and former instructor of criminal justice and constitutional law at Charleston Southern University.

positions.stance: Will "Use the full power of the office to investigate and stop these Financial Bad Guys," such as abusive debt collectors, and join multistate consumer suits.
"I will be the attorney for our beaches, rivers, and water"; will step in when state environmental regulators fall short.
Will bring solicitors together around "tougher, consistent DUI standards" and publicly track plea and conviction rates.
Will "Expand the Attorney General's Violence Against Women prosecution unit" and promote lethality-assessment protocols.
Will build the office's own legal capacity so South Carolina "doesn't need to use insider firms" and review multistate actions the state sat out.

sc-comp-2026-burkhold-mike.name: Mike Burkhold
sc-comp-2026-burkhold-mike.bio: Founder of the healthcare company Equiscript, started in 2009.

positions.stance: Will publish real-time state spending data in "an Online Checkbook anyone can access"; "You shouldn't need a FOIA request to know where your money goes!"
Will challenge agency spending; every dollar "should meet clear standards for legality, necessity, and impact. If it doesn't, I'll stop it and expose it."
Wants to redefine the office "From Bookkeeper to Taxpayer Advocate," bringing "business discipline, common sense, and the courage to say no."

sc-comp-2026-boozer-tiffany.name: Tiffany Boozer
sc-comp-2026-boozer-tiffany.bio: Certified Public Accountant with experience in financial reporting, analysis, and compliance.

positions.stance: Running "to ensure South Carolina's financial records are accurate, reliable, and professionally managed by a certified accounting professional."
"I will execute this office with precision, discipline, and integrity — so South Carolina's finances are trusted."
Committed to ensuring the data behind the state transparency dashboard "is accurate, consistent, and reliable every single month."

sc-supt-2026-weaver-ellen.name: Ellen Weaver
sc-supt-2026-weaver-ellen.bio: South Carolina State Superintendent of Education since 2023 who previously worked for U.S. Senator Jim DeMint.

positions.stance: Emphasizes "laser focus on the fundamentals and well-equipped teachers" and the Palmetto Math Project to improve student achievement.
Fought to secure paid parental leave for teachers, giving educators "time, professional dignity, and respect."
Led a statewide push to train more than 20,000 teachers in evidence-based literacy practices rooted in phonics.
Promised "to pay teachers like professionals," with a path to $50,000 starting pay and compensation rewarding outstanding student outcomes.
Supports strong public schools and champions the Education Scholarship Trust Fund, charters, open enrollment, and microschools.

sc-supt-2026-wright-sylvia.name: Sylvia Wright
sc-supt-2026-wright-sylvia.bio: Educator and Dorchester School District Four coordinator for secondary education; former middle and high school teacher.

positions.stance: Supports meeting students' basic needs and adding social workers, school counselors, and school psychologists in schools statewide.
Supports an enhanced tax credit and childcare vouchers for educators, stronger discipline policies, and reduced excessive standardized testing.
Supports "true school choice options and individualized success pathways," responsible AI use, and expanded Career Technical Education and apprenticeships.
Supports turnaround plans defined by community commissions "rather than top-down state interventions" and rebuilding Department–district relationships.
"Public funds belong in Public Schools"; supports fully funding the system that serves 90% of South Carolina students.

sc-ag-comm-2026-simpson-cody.name: Cody Simpson
sc-ag-comm-2026-simpson-cody.bio: Fifth-generation South Carolina farmer and former South Carolina State Executive Director of the USDA Farm Service Agency.
